_comment: Single source of truth for the /bench and /benchmark suite vocabulary.
Consumed by:
* .github/workflows/bench_baremetal.yml - the `resolve` job reads this file,
matches the requested token against `name` exactly (never by substring),
and refuses anything not declared here;
* scripts/check_bench_suites.py - asserts this file, the workflow_dispatch
`benchmark_suite` choice list, the generated table in docs/BENCHMARKING.md,
and the [[bench]] targets in the crate manifests all agree. Run
`python3 scripts/check_bench_suites.py --write` after editing this file.
Fields:
name       the exact token accepted after /bench or /benchmark.
available  false = declared but not reachable from a slash command; the
refusal message lists it with its `reason` so the gap is stated
rather than silent (AGENTS.md 8.1).
kind       callgrind = needs valgrind + iai-callgrind-runner on the host,
checked before anything runs; wallclock = criterion / custom-main;
counters = needs a usable PMU (`perf stat`), checked by opening a
real counter before anything runs. The kind drives the workflow's
preflight and the Instrument column of the docs table, so a suite
cannot be labelled with an instrument it does not use.
runner     builtin = handled by a named branch of the workflow's case
statement (dual-pass baselines, report post-processing);
generic = run straight from `package` + `target` (+ `env`).
package    cargo package for a generic suite.
target     [[bench]] target name for a generic suite.
env        space-separated KEY=VALUE pairs prefixed to a generic run.
summary    one line, rendered verbatim into the docs table and the
refusal comment. No hardcoded numbers that a run would produce.
arms       required on every callgrind + generic suite; the declaration
scripts/perf_report.py reads to tell our arms from a
third-party baseline. Detection is never inferred from an
arm's name. Fields:
subject_label / baseline_label  words used in the rendered
table headings, e.g. 'Expanse vs Roaring' and the
column header 'vs Roaring (instructions retired, not
time)'. The ratio is published as a bare number under
that header and never narrated in prose.
twins     [{subject, baseline}] - two arms measured over
identical inputs. perf_report.py puts the merge-base
delta and the ratio between them on one row per
subject, and keeps the baseline out of the merge-base
comparison and the regression gate entirely.
One baseline may serve several subjects: where the
competitor exposes a single kernel and we have more
than one path to it (composed vs native), repeating
it is the symmetric comparison, not a duplicate arm.
A subject, by contrast, appears exactly once.
unpaired  our arms with no competitor twin. Listed rather
than assumed, so that adding an arm without saying what
it is fails check_bench_suites.py instead of quietly
entering the report as if it were ours.
check_bench_suites.py asserts the union of twins + unpaired is
exactly the set of functions the suite's
`library_benchmark_group!` declarations name.

suites.name: all
suites.summary: Default for a bare `/bench`: dual-pass Callgrind over `instructions` and `vs_stock`, the two B/key examples, the paired `bench_vs_libjudy` wall-clock comparison, and the fast comparative sweep.

suites.name: extended
suites.summary: Everything in `all`, plus the multi-population scaling sweep and the microarchitecture target-CPU matrix (`bench_report.py --extended --arch-sweep`).

suites.name: vs_stock
suites.summary: C ABI drop-in parity against the stock oracle (`expanse-capi`), dual-pass against the base ref.

suites.name: instructions
suites.summary: Core deterministic Callgrind instruction counters plus the 64-bit and 32-bit B/key examples, dual-pass against the base ref.

suites.name: vs_libjudy
suites.summary: Paired wall-clock comparison of `libexpanse` against a dlopen'd stock libjudy through the identical C surface, arms interleaved per round (`bench_vs_libjudy`).

suites.name: comparative
suites.summary: Wall-clock head-to-head against hashbrown / BTreeMap, with the `bench_report.py --quick` markdown table.

suites.name: ycsb
suites.summary: YCSB core workloads on the 64-bit map.

suites.name: concurrency
suites.summary: `Sync*` wall-clock scaling instrument on a reduced thread/workload sweep; report-only, never gating.

suites.name: point_lookup_counters
suites.summary: Hardware performance counters (`perf stat`) over the random point-lookup path — `probe` minus `build`, with a BCa 95% interval per counter. Diagnostic only: it gates nothing, and it is the instrument the Callgrind `Ir` gate structurally cannot be.

suites.name: search_instructions
suites.summary: Callgrind instruction counters for the inverted-index search kernels, dual-pass against the base ref.

suites.name: smoke_instructions
suites.summary: Scaled-down Callgrind smoke counters, dual-pass against the base ref. The same instrument as the `callgrind-smoke` CI job, on the reference host.

suites.name: search_boolean
suites.summary: Boolean posting-list intersection and union against the search baselines.

suites.name: search_wand
suites.summary: WAND / top-k scoring over the inverted index.

suites.name: search_memory
suites.summary: Live-heap footprint of the inverted index against the search baselines.

suites.name: zset_zadd
suites.summary: Sorted-set insert/update throughput against the skiplist baseline.

suites.name: zset_range
suites.summary: Sorted-set range scans, forward and reverse.

suites.name: zset_rank
suites.summary: Sorted-set rank and select queries.

suites.name: zset_memory
suites.summary: Live-heap footprint of the sorted-set representation against the skiplist baseline.

suites.name: hashbrown_native_suite
suites.summary: Core point-operation comparison against hashbrown.

suites.name: hashbrown_ycsb
suites.summary: YCSB workloads run on the hashbrown comparison arms.

suites.name: hashbrown_tail_latency
suites.summary: Tail-latency percentiles against hashbrown, including rehash spikes.

suites.name: hashbrown_container_dists
suites.summary: Key-distribution sensitivity sweep against hashbrown.

suites.name: hashbrown_memory_alloc
suites.summary: Live-heap and allocation-count comparison against hashbrown.

suites.name: large_values
suites.summary: Blob-arena storage paths for values above the immediate capacity.

suites.name: rocksdb
suites.summary: RocksDB pluggable MemTable: fillrandom / readrandom / seek / scan and RAM bytes-per-key against a fair variable-height skiplist baseline (`integrations/rocksdb`, C++ built against release libexpanse).

suites.name: embedded
suites.summary: 32-bit embedded trie surface (`trie32` / `set32` / `map32` / `blobmap32`).

suites.name: batch_lookup
suites.summary: Interleave-width sweep for the batched descent, on a cold-DRAM population and a cache-resident control.

suites.name: compare
suites.summary: Standing container comparison harness across the core map and set types.

suites.name: bench_llm_datastore
suites.reason: needs the generated corpus under `docs/benchmarks/llm_inference/data/`, which is materialized by that suite's Python driver; run `docs/benchmarks/llm_inference/run.sh` instead.
suites.summary: Speculative-decoding datastore against a static sorted window index.

suites.name: bench_grammar_masks
suites.reason: part of the same Python-driven pipeline as `bench_llm_datastore` and reports into its JSON artifacts; run `docs/benchmarks/llm_inference/run.sh` instead.
suites.summary: Grammar-constrained decoding mask cache and set algebra against roaring and dense bitmaps.
